result.title: SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Speculative Decoding (SD) has demonstrated its efficacy in accelerating large language model inference, but for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the diverse input modalities make it difficult for a small trained drafter to achieve consistently high throughput. Self-speculative decoding reuses parts of the target model as a drafter which retains the multi-modal capability of the VLMs, yet its efficiency depends on choosing a suitable draft configuration for each prompt. We propose Single-Peak SPeculative decoding (SP$^2$ec), a training-free bandit algorithm that adapts the draft configuration during generation. SP$^2$ec exploits the single-peak throughput pattern observed in existing self-speculative methods, including SWIFT, KnapSpec, SpecVLM, and our simple cosSim. Our algorithmic design explicitly minimizes a novel notion of wall-time regret for each given query, corresponding to the empirical wall-time latency. Theoretical guarantees on the wall-time regret show that SP$^2$ec can exploit the optimal draft configuration, with negligible exploration cost. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B across visual and textual tasks show consistent improvements of up to 11\% over the original self-speculative methods, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed SP$^2$ec algorithm.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的 bandit 算法 SP²ec，在生成过程中自适应选择自推测解码的 draft 配置，利用已有自推测方法的单峰吞吐模式，以最小化 wall-time regret 为目标，在 Qwen2.5-VL 与 LLaVA-NeXT 上比原始方法最高提升约 11% 吞吐。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文不涉及 latent 推理状态或视觉证据使用，与 LVR 主线无直接关系；但其用 bandit 在线选择计算配置、以实际 wall-time 为目标并给出 regret 保证的思路，可能为 LVR 中动态计算预算分配与停止决策的成本建模提供可核查的借鉴线索。
